In summary, our research is concerned with
developing a framework for assessing the economic impacts of alternative fire-hazard-reducing policies on the production of saw logs and biomass from the forests of the Pacific Northwest.
the effects of fire-hazard-reducing treatments on the supply and mix of biomass and saw logs.
the development of a spatially explicit, dynamic model of forest biomass and wood supply for fire-hazard-reductions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, for the area studied, the three policy scenarios resulted in similar mixtures of species and sizes of saw logs and dirty chips removed from the landscape.
the mix of species and tree sizes removed under each of the three scenarios was surprisingly similar.

the mix of species and size of both dirty chip and saw log removed is surprisingly similar among scenarios, but the Min Merch scenario removed more saw logs in midsize classes (7 to 10in. (17-8 to 25.4cm) and 10 to 16 in. (25.4 to40.6cm)) and more noncommercial species than the other two.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
fire-hazard-reduced stands in the study area will contain large amounts of biomass and saw logs.
, for the area studied, the three policy scenarios considered would remove a large volume of dirty chips and saw logs, with a relatively minor component from trees less than 7in dbh.
fire-hazard-reductions treatments are likely to remove large quantities of dirty chips and saw logs from the region, but the exact quantities will be highly dependent upon policy.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, although the mix of species and size classes removed is not very sensitive to the policy scenario, the total volume removed is very sensitive to the scenario and the total volume removed can be quite large.
the mix of species and size classes removed from a fire-hazard-reduced area is surprisingly similar, even though the area treated under different scenarios can vary by 80%.
fire-hazard-reductions treatments can be designed to meet multiple objectives, such as improving fire-hazard conditions while also providing a source of biomass and/or saw logs.
